correctness.rationale: For any finite connected simple H and any m>=1 internally disjoint 4-edge ears joining old vertices at H-distance 2 (including repeated endpoint pairs), replacing ear excursions by old length-2 paths proves the old graph distances remain exact. Sending each ear private vertex to a chosen old common neighbor gives a 1-Lipschitz retraction of filtered vertex-sampled graph powers. At r=1, each ear adds a relative circle. At r=2, the center link is precisely the induced square on b,x,y,d and that square bounds a cone at the chosen common old neighbor; removing each center splits off an S^2. After all centers are removed, b,d are dominated by the chosen neighbor. At every r>=3 the centers too are dominated and all ears collapse away. Naturality of the retraction plus explicit nullhomologies yields exact new bars 3m H0[0,1), m H1[1,2), m H2[2,3). Independent BFS and mod-2 clique-chain enumeration checked 4 host/ear cases, including duplicated and overlapping endpoints; the universal assertion uses the domination and link argument, not these tests.

originality.rationale: The local four-edge ear surgery with arbitrary connected host and repeated/overlapping ears was not found as a corollary of the inspected graph-Rips and metric-gluing primary formulations. Three-edge theta graph and finite projective-plane incidence graphs have similar H1/H2 paired timing, but a different graph metric and no universal old-graph retraction under an ear operation. The Adamaszek et al gluing theorem imposes intersection/short-path hypotheses, not verified to imply this exact operation. The published statements inspected do not establish the claimed arbitrary-host persistence splitting; best-of-knowledge priority remains qualified.
